summary: Wooden fire tower on Beacon Pole Hill, Cumberland RI, first operated 1920 and removed 1935; the hill is better known for a Revolutionary War beacon.

facts.status_note: The former-lookout register says the tower was removed in 1935; no source describes any remains of it today.

notes_for_editor: Only one source (the former-lookout register) covers the 1920-1935 wooden tower. Two searches and the local history pages gave no staffing, fire or design detail. The colonial beacon and the 1897 replica are documented but are not the fire tower; keep them separate. An unverified Facebook post claims a late-1960s Boy Scout commemorative tower on the hill; not used. Elevation conflict: 450 ft (register) vs 556 ft (BVHS, Valley Breeze). The Valley Breeze article has no dateline in the text we read. Its reader comments are dated March 26 and April 4, 2023, and its URL ID was created in March 2023, so the story dates it to 2023. The article reports council funding toward a purchase that was still pending, not a completed sale. Check the Catamint Brook purchase status before publishing.
